transcript.content: It's for my mum, Margaret, 84. She has osteoarthritis in both knees, type 2 diabetes, and her eyesight is poor from macular degeneration.
Most mornings I help her sit up and swing her legs out; it takes 10-15 minutes because her knees are stiff. At night I help her into bed.
She can get to the toilet in the day but slowly with her frame. At night she gets up about twice and has been unsteady.
She can't get in or out of the bath anymore. I help her have a strip wash at the sink 4-5 times a week, about 30 minutes.
She needs help with socks, shoes and buttons because she can't bend and her fingers are stiff. About 15 minutes each morning.
She uses a frame indoors and holds the rail on the stairs; I walk behind her on the stairs.
She fell twice in the bathroom since spring, last time in August. She couldn't get up on her own and pressed her alarm pendant.
She can eat but I cut up meat for her as she can't see it well.
I fill a dosette box weekly; she has missed doses of metformin when I didn't remind her.
She can't read letters because of her eyes; I read her post to her.
She used to go to church on Sundays; she'd need someone to take her and help her in and out of the car.
Not confused, but I worry about her falling when alone.
At night she gets up about twice for the toilet, each time 10 minutes, and she's unsteady.
No, nobody needs to be awake watching her all night.

answers.29: I have osteoarthritis in both knees, which are very stiff in the morning. Most mornings my daughter helps me sit up and swing my legs out of bed. This takes 10 to 15 minutes. At night she helps me get into bed.
answers.30: In the day I can get to the toilet slowly using my walking frame. At night I get up about twice to use the toilet and I am unsteady on my feet.
answers.31: I can no longer get in or out of the bath. My daughter helps me have a strip wash at the sink 4 to 5 times a week. Each wash takes about 30 minutes.
answers.32: I can't bend to put on socks and shoes, and my fingers are too stiff for buttons. My daughter helps me dress every morning. This takes about 15 minutes.
answers.33: I use a walking frame indoors. On the stairs I hold the rail and my daughter walks behind me in case I fall.
answers.34: I have fallen twice in the bathroom since spring. The last fall was in August. I could not get up on my own and had to press my alarm pendant for help.
answers.35: I can feed myself, but because of my poor eyesight I can't see my food well, so my daughter cuts up meat for me.
answers.36: My daughter fills a dosette box for me every week. I have missed doses of my diabetes medicine (metformin) when she has not reminded me.
answers.37: I can't read letters because of macular degeneration. My daughter reads my post to me.
answers.39: I used to go to church on Sundays. To go now I would need someone to take me and help me in and out of the car.
answers.40: I am not confused, but I am at risk of falling when I am on my own.
answers.42: I get up about twice a night to use the toilet. Each time takes about 10 minutes and I am unsteady.

checklist: Repeat prescription list from the GP surgery
Any letters from the eye clinic about macular degeneration
Record of the alarm pendant call-outs (ask the provider)
Any physiotherapy or occupational therapy reports
A short care diary for one week (what help, how long, day and night)
draft.gp_letter:
Dear Dr Patel,

My mother, Margaret Sample (DOB 03/04/1941), is applying for Attendance Allowance. Please could you provide a brief letter confirming her diagnoses (osteoarthritis of both knees, type 2 diabetes, macular degeneration) and, if you are able to, how they affect her ability to wash, dress, move around safely and manage her medicines. She has had two falls since spring.

Thank you,
Jane Sample (daughter)
draft.carer_statement: I am Margaret's daughter and I see her every day. She has osteoarthritis in both knees, type 2 diabetes and macular degeneration. I help her get out of and into bed, wash at the sink, dress, and cut up her food. I fill her dosette box weekly and read her post to her. She has fallen twice since spring and could not get up alone.
notes_for_user: Add how long Mum has had each condition and her medicine doses (page 7).
Confirm the date of the last fall.
Tick 'Yes' on each question listed below; we can't tick boxes for you in this version.
Add the NI number, bank details, signature and date yourself.
